Where is the best coffee on Koh Samui? | Bophut and Fisherman's Village have the most cafés, with Chaweng, Lamai and Maenam close behind. Several small specialty roasters work in Maenam and Bophut, many using Thai arabica from the northern highlands. Look for a grinder on the counter and beans with a roast date, and check opening days, as many small cafés close one or two days a week.
Are there laptop-friendly cafés on Samui? | Yes, especially in Bophut, Chaweng, Lamai and Maenam, and most have free Wi-Fi. Speeds and power sockets vary, so ask before settling in, order something every hour or two, and carry a Thai SIM as a hotspot backup. For calls and long days, a coworking day pass is more reliable.
How much is a coffee on Koh Samui? | About 40–60 THB for a Thai iced coffee from a street stall, 60–100 THB at a local café, 90–150 THB for a specialty latte and up to about 230 THB at upmarket cafés in 2026. Resort coffee costs about 150–250 THB plus service and VAT.
Where can I get breakfast early before a tour pickup? | Ask your hotel for an early or boxed breakfast, as most independent cafés open only at 07:00–08:00. 7-Eleven is open 24 hours for toasties and iced coffee, and Thai breakfast stalls near markets sell rice porridge and fried dough sticks from about 06:00.
What is Thai iced coffee? | Strong coffee, traditionally brewed through a cloth filter, poured over ice with sweetened condensed and evaporated milk (kafae yen), or black and sweet (oliang). It is very sweet by default: ask for "wan noi" for less sugar or "mai wan" for none.
Are there vegan cafés on Koh Samui? | Yes, especially in Lamai and Bophut, where health cafés serve plant-based breakfasts, smoothie bowls and juices for the island's yoga and fitness crowd. Most cafés offer oat or soy milk. In Thai cafés, ask for "mai sai nom" (no milk), because Thai iced coffee comes with condensed milk by default.
Are there cafés with a sea view on Koh Samui? | Yes. The beach road in Fisherman's Village has cafés looking across to Koh Phangan, and The Jungle Club above Chaweng Noi has a hillside view over Chaweng Bay, reached by a very steep road. Beach-club brunches at Nikki Beach on the west coast add sea views.
Can I pay by card in cafés on Samui? | In most modern cafés, yes, by card or Thai QR payment; small local cafés and street stalls are often cash only. Carry small notes, and if a card terminal offers to charge you in your home currency, choose THB.
